text:
jess-support: Hi team — customer experiencing repeated 429s and spikes in latency when switching between models. They say it started after a bursty batch job yesterday evening. Posting logs and repro.

jess-support: Root error snippet from customer (redacted keys): 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 23:02:14 GMT
x-request-id: req_abc123
content-type: application/json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "rate limit exceeded for model rwd-infer-13b-v2",
    "code": 429,
    "details": "per-model tpm/rpm exceeded or concurrency limit reached"
  }
}
```

jess-support: Customer says they were hitting ~520 req/min for that model with mixed short completions and long-context evals (~32k tokens). They also saw auth failures intermittently: 
```
{ "error": "authentication failed: billing issue" }
```

maya-support: Thanks @jess-support — is this for a Hosted account or Dedicated? Any dedicated pools pinned to rwd-infer-13b-v2? Also need the project id.

jess-support: Hosted (project rwd-cust-881). No dedicated. They used streaming endpoints and some concurrent SDK clients (node) with default retry backoff. They attached a curl repro that reliably gets a 429 in ~20-30s: 
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.infer/v1/completions \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-infer-13b-v2","input":"test","max_tokens":1024,"stream":false}'
```

jess-support: Repro steps they used: 1) start 8 parallel workers 2) each sends ~1 req/sec for 10 minutes 3) every 2 min one worker sends a very long-context request (context ~30k tokens) 4) observe 429s and 500ms->2s p50->p95 latency spikes.

simon-eng: My initial thought: two things colliding — per-model RPM/TPM caps + context-length related throttling. Long-context (30k) requests are heavier and may reduce available concurrency; runtime might apply model-specific token rate limits which are stricter for long contexts. Do we have the actual per-model limits for rwd-infer-13b-v2? @rate-limit-bot?

rate-limit-bot: Automated response: rwd-infer-13b-v2 limits (hosted): per-project RPM=600, TPM=18000, max_concurrency=16, long-context (>=16k) throttling factor=2 (applies to effective concurrency). See docs/limits.

ingrid-product: If the bot numbers are right — 8 workers at ~1 rps = 480 req/min already close to RPM but long-context bursts will count higher toward TPM due to token cost. Also the runtime marks long-context requests as costing 2x concurrency for scheduling, so hitting max_concurrency is likely. Customer's pattern (periodic 30k token calls) will produce big TPM bursts.

alex-sre: Also note: customer reported intermittent auth failures — I pulled logs for project rwd-cust-881. There was a payment method failure event around 2026-03-02T23:00:01Z (billing-bot flagged), which pushed the account into a soft-limited state for ~7 minutes while retries attempted. During that window our gateway returned 401/402 for some requests, and clients retried with backoff, creating retry storms that bump effective RPM. I'll paste upstream correlational snippet: 
```
2026-03-02T23:00:01Z billing-service: payment_failure project=rwd-cust-881 method=card ending=4242
2026-03-02T23:00:10Z auth-gateway: token_validate status=failed project=rwd-cust-881
2026-03-02T23:01:15Z api-gateway: incoming_req project=rwd-cust-881 path=/v1/completions model=rwd-infer-13b-v2 count=180
```

alex-sre: That retry behavior plus long-context heavy calls likely pushed them over both RPM and TPM and then into concurrency queuing leading to 429 responses.

maya-support: Good find. Customer is on standard tier, which doesn't allow burst override. Proposed next steps for support thread: 1) confirm quota metrics with customer (I can pull per-minute metrics), 2) suggest quick mitigations (reduce concurrent workers to <=4, increase inter-request jitter, avoid >16k context unless necessary), 3) offer canary to a thinner model variant (rwd-infer-7b-quant) for long-context workloads, 4) propose upgrade path (dedicated pool or higher quota) if they need sustained throughput.

jess-support: I shared that with customer; they asked for concrete numbers — can we give an explanation of how TPM is computed (tokens in + tokens out) and how long-context requests factor into effective concurrency? Also they asked why some requests returned 401/402 previously.

simon-eng: TPM = sum of input_tokens + output_tokens per minute. Long-context increases input_tokens massively; streaming outputs also contribute as tokens are emitted. Effective concurrency uses a scheduler weight: weight = max(1, ceil(context_tokens / 8192) * throttle_factor). For rwd-infer-13b-v2 throttle_factor=2 so a 30k-context request => ceil(30000/8192)=4 => weight=4*2=8 effective concurrency, meaning it can saturate the 16 max_concurrency quickly.

simon-eng: 401/402 were due to billing-service failing validation and the auth gateway returning 401 for token validation, not a model throttle. Billing failure caused temporary auth rejection; after payment retry it allowed traffic but the client retries had already amplified traffic.

ingrid-product: For the customer-facing reply let's be explicit: 1) Provide per-model numbers (RPM/TPM/concurrency) and the formula for effective concurrency and TPM calculation. 2) Give immediate mitigations (lower parallelism, jitter, move long-context to off-peak, or use a cheaper model for long context). 3) Offer to run a short baseline with us (we can simulate their pattern from our infra) or open a dedicated trial if they expect sustained throughput.

maya-support: I'll draft the reply. Also asking Eng/SRE if we can add a temporary leniency: can we grant a 10-minute burst window to avoid throttling while they fix the billing? @alex-sre

alex-sre: We can temporarily raise RPM by 30% for 10 minutes per account via the rate-limiter admin UI, but only for accounts without active fraud flags. Since billing shows a failure, ops policy is to not lift until billing resolved. We can, however, whitelist a limited set of IPs or give an opt-in canary to a different model variant if they accept a guided migration.

jess-support: Customer accepted mitigations: reduced concurrency to 3, added jitter, and switched long-context calls to rwd-infer-7b-quant for testing. They also fixed billing method. Will monitor and report back.

maya-support: I'll close the escalation once we see stable metrics for 30 minutes. For the internal follow-ups: 1) Document this pattern in support KB: "Long-context bursts + retry storms => TPS/RPM/TMP exhaustion" 2) Consider improving billing-failure handling (avoid auth 401s during transient card retries) to prevent retry storms. 3) Add a small dashboard for per-project effective_concurrency metric.

rate-limit-bot: Reminder: docs updated: https://docs.redwood.infer/limits#per-model and internal KB at /kb/long-context-retries

jess-support: Thanks everyone. I'll paste customer confirmation when they report post-change stability. :thumbsup:
